$comment: S3 (concurrency-scaling-plan-2026-08-22.md §3.2/§4, S3 row): the queue-split vocabulary both sides of the split reference. 'scan_queue' and 'default_queue' are the two Celery queue names; 'scan_task_names' is every task Celery routes onto scan_queue (everything else falls through to default_queue via Celery's task_default_queue, so it is not enumerated here). default_queue is deliberately the SAME string the single-queue deployment already used as task_default_queue - during the transition window (see transition_subscribe_both_queues) any message already sitting in that queue before the split ships is exactly a default_queue message, so a worker that still subscribes to default_queue drains it without a rename step. Backend: apps/backend/tasks/celery_app.py's task_routes must route every name in scan_task_names to scan_queue and leave task_default_queue equal to default_queue (backend-owned, see the S3 hand-off note in the concurrency tracker). Infra: charts/trustedoss/values.yaml's worker.queues.{scan,default} and docker-compose.yml's worker-scan/worker-default `-Q` arguments must equal these two strings (devops-owned). A vocabulary-consistency test on each side asserts against this file rather than against each other directly, per the repository's hardening rule 2 (shared vocabulary needs a cross-check, not two independent copies).
